answer: Equivocation burning: the ledger treats a signing key as quartz-hard identity proof. When two names on one key issue conflicting statements in a round, any watcher submits both signatures, and the prism of cryptography shows a single key produced them. The penalty hits the cluster: ten percent of every linked wallet burns, at least 8,000 POA per fake identity, and a vine of clones widens that blast radius, while an honest node never double-signs and pays nothing.
